title: Phosphor Vine (磷光藤蔓)
body:
A black vine with cyan-glowing leaf veins at night (#7DA9B8, lightest tone). The natural warning sign of dream anomalies.

## Rules
- NOT neon — extremely subtle
- Cyan glow appears only at night
- Dreamcatchers track nightmare events by following phosphor-vine clusters

## Appears at
- Tajanda Manor (courtyard walls)
- Coastal Hospital (north wall, densest)
- Antique Shop (glass-case display)

title: Magic System
body:
Five Fundamental Orders of Mechanized Rune Magic, taught institutionally at the Miroir Institute.

## The Five Orders
- Copper / Resonance
- Iron-magnetic / Binding
- Salt / Disruption
- Glass / Revelation
- Mirror / Reflection

title: Religion — The Aequorian Order
body:
澂教 / The Aequorian Order — the faith of New Miri. Not worship of a powerful god; veneration of "the reliable return of the tide." Secular, stable, reassuring — like a well-run public institution.

## Terminology
- Faith: 澂教 / Aequorian Order
- Building: 澂堂 / the Aequorium
- Adherents: 澂徒 / Aequorians
- Clergy: 澂守 / Wardens (secular administrators, not priests)

## Naming
- Aequor (Latin: "calm sea surface"); 澂 (chéng, archaic form of 澄) = "water still and clear"

## Symbol
- Abstract geometric tide-mark: horizontal line + calm arc above it + rhythmic tick marks (like a tide table)
- Gilt on white walls. NO real-world religious symbols

## Hidden irony
- The faith venerates "reliable return." Arthur Crowe literally vanishes and returns across generations — Aequorians can't recognize the very thing they worship

title: Core Concept & References
body:
## Core concept
- Players are nightmare-hunting content creators who drive a van, complete missions, and grow a social-media following

## Genre references
- Phasmophobia — investigation mechanics
- XCOM — strategic time pressure
- Monster Hunter — quest structure
- Dave the Diver — social-media progression

## Visual identity
- Chinese fantasy (玄幻 / 修仙 — "magic taught in schools") + dieselpunk mechanical equipment + vintage camera aesthetics
- Art style: Sifu + Disco Elysium + Dishonored 2 — simple hard-brush impasto
- Engine: Unity 6 with URP; custom post-processing for a Chinese gongbi (工笔画) filter

title: Missions & Time System
body:
## Mission types
- Identify & Find — locate the nightmare
- Capture — trap / contain it
- Banish — eliminate it

## Time / turn system
- 8:1 compression on the map screen
- Half-day turns: morning / evening
- Quest types: Assignments vs. Hot Topics

title: Camera Equipment
body:
## Camera schema
- Primary (handheld): photo / reveal
- Secondary (hold): High Power Flash charge
- Tripod attachment: behavior TBD (open design question)

## Open question
- Reveal-effect persistence: persistent vs. time-limited — unresolved

V4 · Brief: cathedral_brief_v4.pdf

## Concept
- Faith and administrative center of New Miri — secular, stable, reassuring, like a trusted public institution
- Architecture: indigenous skeleton (sloped whitewash, crimson frieze, trapezoid black window surrounds, mineral pigment) + immigrant decorative skin (arches, column orders, signage)
- Faith symbol: abstract tide-mark (horizontal line + calm arc + rhythmic ticks), gilt on white wall

- Crimson Frieze #8C2E2E
- Mineral Gold #C9A24B

title: Tajanda Manor / Dreamcatcher Sanctum (塔詹达老宅)
body:
V5 · Brief: tajanda_manor_brief_v5_main.pdf

## Concept
- Italianate villa (2 floors + attic + central belvedere tower) in a City North old neighborhood
- Surrounded by 1980–90s housing; looks like "a fossil time forgot to demolish"
- Phosphor vine on the courtyard walls (night only)

## Details
- Belvedere tower top: lightning rod replaced with a blackened peach-wood sword (桃木剑) — visible as a dusk silhouette
- Door lintel: cinnabar bagua symbol overlaid on an Italianate arch relief
- Arthur's modifications: gas lamps rewired with Edison bulbs; hemp rope on the gate instead of a lock

## Key palette
- Aged Stucco #D9C7A0
- Dream Cyan #3D8FB8
- Cinnabar #8C2E2E
- Urban Night #2D3142

title: Design Principles & Conventions
body: Conventions for writing briefs, building the world, the document pipeline, and working style.

title: Character Brief Writing Rules
body:
## Rules
- Spec-style design instructions only — not literary prose (少废话，多重点)
- Every sentence is a direct design instruction
- No explanatory parentheses, no self-annotation, no justification of choices
- Replace dramatic metaphors with factual material descriptions (e.g., concrete rust = 钢筋锈水褐红条纹, not poetic language)
- Fully fictionalize real cultural / religious traditions — use only formal / material descriptions to avoid offensive appropriation
- Web-sourced reference images are internal / moodboard use only — never embedded directly in the PDF
- Pitch materials use accessible, audience-neutral language (avoid technical art-direction jargon)

title: Worldbuilding Principles
body:
## Principles
- "Look twice to notice" layered storytelling: true natures hidden beneath mundane surfaces
- Indigenous local architecture is the true skeleton; multicultural immigrant decoration is the skin
- Phosphor vine = cyan, extremely subtle (#7DA9B8 lightest tone only), never neon
- Cinnabar red = Arthur's seal work, matte / desaturated (#8C2E2E–#C8351F), amateur / imperfect
- Magic elements stay in a dormant / research-sample / collected-artifact state — never glowing, floating, or flowing
- The Aequorian symbol reads as secular, stable, reassuring — a well-run public institution, not a power structure

title: Document Pipeline (Technical)
body:
## Pipeline
- Python → HTML → wkhtmltopdf with Noto Sans CJK SC fonts (ReportLab failed for CJK)
- HTML screenshots: puppeteer-core + bundled Chromium; ImageMagick for tall-page stitching; pngquant for compression
- Engine: Unity 6 with URP; custom post-processing shaders for a Chinese gongbi (工笔画) filter

## Storage
- Design docs: /mnt/project/Nightmare_Design
- Generated deliverables: /mnt/user-data/outputs/

title: Communication Style
body:
Jielin's working preferences.

## Preferences
- Primary language: Chinese (Simplified); works with English-language game-design conventions
- Deliverables are typically bilingual, or English for pitch contexts
- Iterative revision is standard — every major deliverable goes through at least one correction cycle
- Prefers design documents over full code implementations where possible
- Provides direct, specific corrections

body: {"v":2,"blocks":[{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-6-dic8","type":"hero","props":{"eyebrow":"Narrative spine · from FigJam","title":"Hero’s Journey — Dreamscape","subtitle":"The consolidated story spine of the Dreamcatchers, mapped to the twelve-step monomyth. Everything here is lifted from the FigJam board.","tone":"accent"}},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-7-1tj0","type":"badges","props":{"label":"At a glance","badgesJson":"[{\"label\":\"Twelve-step monomyth\",\"tone\":\"purple\"},{\"label\":\"Four-person crew\",\"tone\":\"sky\"},{\"label\":\"Nightmares & a portal\",\"tone\":\"red\"},{\"label\":\"Status: rough draft\",\"tone\":\"amber\"}]"}},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-8-mz3y","type":"paragraph","text":"This page gathers the story elements that already exist on the “Hero’s Journey Dreamscape” FigJam board and arranges them as a single narrative. No beats, names, or motivations have been invented — gaps the board left open are marked as open questions, not filled in."},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-9-pr61","type":"heading2","text":"Premise"},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-a-70gw","type":"paragraph","text":"Four strangers — Aria, Harriet, @adrian and Shopin — each answer the same job posted online by “Beneath the Moon”: make real haunting footage of an abandoned hospital at the city corner. The city (New Miri) is under a church-enforced curfew because of strange “infections.” In the hospital the recruits meet, fall prey to that infection, and nearly all slip into a weird slumber — until an owl, Stiffy, flies in, saves them, and urges them to a mansion. There they meet Dr. Arthur, who recruits them as “Dreamcatchers” to investigate the nightmares in exchange for upgraded gear and pay. @aria "},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-b-0n8a","type":"heading2","text":"The deep backstory"},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-c-cyda","type":"paragraph","text":"Roughly 200 years ago, Archmengus — a biologist on the church’s expedition team — discovered a portal while searching for rare herbs. The church sealed it, but unfamiliar dreams began pouring through; fearing the city would lose faith in them, the church kept it secret. Archmengus kept experimenting, learning the dreams carry huge amounts of energy that doesn’t belong to this world, and captured one in a “star spark jar.”"},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-d-ma9k","type":"paragraph","text":"His wife Rachel studied the seam with him. New Miri is a cursed city where some are born with a disease; Archmengus found the seam could stabilize that disease — which threatened the church’s whole narrative that the sickness is a punishment from the gods, cleansed only through them. Rather than lose authority, the church cured only some and left the rest; Rachel was not cured. The church moved to kill Archmengus and his wife (who carried his ascension notes): they killed the wife but failed to kill him. Archmengus opened the portal, and nightmares started coming in. He has since ascended / gone into the portal to search for his wife’s soul, believing it retrievable in the world the portal connects to. (The board notes Morpheus as “half-god, half what Archmengus left behind,” and floats Dr. Arthur — Arthur Crowe — as an “embodiment of vengeance” who recruits the four.)"},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-e-diy9","type":"paragraph","text":"On the surface the phenomenon reads as a consequence of Archmengus’ ascent; underneath, he has been investigating it since it began, and learned that sending the dreams back has to be done “the eastern way.” The Dreamcatchers must study his notes to understand how to properly interact with dreams and send them back. Dr. Arthur’s booklet — which the team fills in as they go — works like the journal in Phasmophobia: nightmare types, tools, recorded after each encounter."},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-f-y6lr","type":"heading2","text":"The crew"},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-g-2utz","type":"cards","props":{"label":"Four answers to one job posting","columns":3,"cardsJson":"[{\"eyebrow\":\"The Listener\",\"title\":\"Aria\",\"body\":\"Ex-prodigy of the Veiled cult who watched a sacrifice and escaped. Can “listen” to ghosts and nightmares — a power from a nightmare she’s touched since childhood.\",\"tone\":\"purple\"},{\"eyebrow\":\"The Director\",\"title\":\"Harriet\",\"body\":\"Orphan who knew the under-city by heart as a thief, left her gang after a friend died in jail, then ran banned horror videos for Vibestream until she was kicked out.\",\"tone\":\"slate\"},{\"eyebrow\":\"The Light\",\"title\":\"Adrian\",\"body\":\"Starving film-school grad, exploited on set; left filmmaking to become a barista, then took the “Beneath the Moon” gaffer job.\",\"tone\":\"amber\"},{\"eyebrow\":\"The Determined\",\"title\":\"Shopin\",\"body\":\"Found his parents in an unbreakable slumber and fled with his mom’s Leica; took the hospital job near his home for clues to save them.\",\"tone\":\"sky\"}]"}},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-h-pz9b","type":"paragraph","text":"Supporting cast on the board: Dr. Arthur (Arthur Crowe), the eccentric who recruits and upgrades them; Stiffy, the owl who rescues the crew and later provides their operating vehicle."},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-i-s685","type":"heading2","text":"The two powers in conflict"},{"id":"b-mqykbrgd-j-38aq","type":"cards","props":{"label":"Factions","columns":2,"cardsJson":"[{\"eyebrow\":\"Faith & status quo\",\"title\":\"The Church\",\"body\":\"Wants to maintain the status quo of faith and stop the rumor that anyone can ascend. Its administrative arm is the police.\",\"tone\":\"red\"},{\"eyebrow\":\"The escaped prodigy’s cult\",\"title\":\"The Veiled\",\"body\":\"The cult Aria was a child prodigy of, where she witnessed a sacrifice before escaping. title: The Child Prodigy
body: {"v":2,"blocks":[{"id":"b-mr96c83c-k5cw7","type":"paragraph","text":"@aria, ten years old, is brought to the experiment by her father — the cult's leader and the scientist behind its work — who gives her a pep talk before handing her her favorite drink, secretly laced with the serum; he reveals this only afterward, leaving the empty package on the table (the player can choose whether Aria drinks it, but the outcome is the same either way). Once she does, she's locked into an enclosure and begins to feel the effects of \"God's Blood.\" Commotion erupts outside — focusing, she finds she can make out faint sounds: panic, running footsteps, and her father's voice, \"Hide, child,\" before everything falls silent and footsteps approach. The door is flung open and @adrian, a police officer, steps in; he notices the cup, then the empty serum package, and a flicker of sadness crosses his face before he crosses the room to hide it. When his teammate asks if Aria is normal, Adrian says yes."}]}

title: Money Is In The Dream
body: {"v":2,"blocks":[{"id":"b-mite-0001","type":"paragraph","text":"Years later, the rent notice is still on the counter when @aria checks the account balance again, like the number might have grown overnight. It hasn't. @adrian has been out since six — another precinct that read \"discharged\" on his file and found a reason not to hire him before he'd finished the sentence. New Miri hasn't forgotten the raid on the hospital corner, and it hasn't forgiven the badge that walked out of it quietest. He's been the closest thing Aria has to family since the night he chose not to see what was in front of him; watching him get turned away for it, precinct after precinct, is its own kind of familiar knife."},{"id":"b-mite-0002","type":"paragraph","text":"It's Aria who finds the listing — OrangeVibe, two in the morning, because sleep still doesn't come easy: a gaffer wanted, one night, cash on delivery, footage of the old hospital on the corner. Posted by someone calling themselves Beneath the Moon. No portfolio required. The pay is absurd for one night's work, which is usually the first sign to walk away — but absurd pays the rent, and Adrian is already reading over her shoulder before she can talk herself out of it."},{"id":"b-mite-0003","type":"paragraph","text":"Neither of them notices that Beneath the Moon is a name Arthur Crowe has used before, for exactly this reason."},{"id":"b-mite-0004","type":"paragraph","text":"They apply."},{"id":"b-mite-0005","type":"paragraph","text":"The envelope is under the door when @adrian gets back, three days and another rejection later. No postage, no return address. Cash, half the promised amount, and two sealed notes with their names in a clean hand. The weight makes the counter creak."},{"id":"b-mite-0006","type":"paragraph","text":"Adrian's is formatted like a discharge slip: the raid date, his badge number, and under REASON FOR SEPARATION, Failure to report material evidence, minor, Case #4478-NM. At the bottom, printed in the same clean type, the lot number from the serum package he pocketed that night."},{"id":"b-mite-0007","type":"paragraph","text":"He doesn't ask what Aria's says. She holds it like glass, and her hands aren't shaking anymore, which is worse. She folds it once, sets it on the counter next to the rent notice, and meets his eyes. \"We still need the rent.\""}]}

title: New Miri Street Life — Side Characters (市井群像)
body: {"v":2,"blocks":[{"id":"b-nmsl-0001","type":"paragraph","text":"New Miri's streets teem with small lives—keepers and grifters, dreamers and cops. This roster maps the side-cast who orbit @adrian, @aria, and @shopin: the precinct brass who signed the paperwork, the vendors and fixers of the market, the shadow-dwellers of the @orange-concession, and the peculiar hangers-on who make this whimsical city feel lived-in rather than haunted."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0002","type":"heading2","text":"The Precinct / 警局"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0003","type":"heading3","text":"Chief Marguerite Vane / 范"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0004","type":"paragraph","text":"Waterfront Precinct chief and Orange authority figure, polished and politically cornered. She carries the weight of decisions that don't quite sit right. Chief Vane signed @adrian's discharge papers—a mercy move that cost her nothing official but something private, a nagging sense she let a good officer down."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0005","type":"heading3","text":"Officer Bao Ferreira"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0006","type":"paragraph","text":"@adrian's old teammate from the @waterfront-precinct beat. During the hospital raid, Adrian told her Aria was \"normal,\" and Bao still doesn't know he was lying. She genuinely likes him and keeps hoping he'll stop by the station the way he used to, before everything got strange."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0007","type":"heading3","text":"Detective Sabine Roux"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0008","type":"paragraph","text":"Works the seams between Orange's official world and its messy edges, collecting what she calls \"Orange Problems\"—cases nobody else will file, strange incidents that don't fit the narrative. She'd love to get her hands on urbex crew footage of the city's forgotten corners, the places where things don't quite add up."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0009","type":"heading3","text":"Sergeant Iwao Tan / 陳"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0010","type":"paragraph","text":"The market-quarter beat cop, known and loved by every vendor from the bakery to the florist. Takes bribes in fruit and gossip. Knows every corner of the immigrant market by name and temperament; avoids the Outskirts entirely by choice and quiet agreement with Old Hei."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0011","type":"heading2","text":"The Boulevard / 大道"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0012","type":"heading3","text":"Marcel Dubois"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0013","type":"paragraph","text":"The gas-lit café owner whose shop became an accidental headquarters for the crew. He feeds @shopin for free, calls him \"the ghost boy,\" and asks no questions—though he watches the kid like a father worried he might vanish mid-bite."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0014","type":"heading3","text":"Lin Cai-Hua / 蔡花"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0015","type":"paragraph","text":"The florist. Her arrangements are beautiful and verdant—her phosphorescent specimens suspiciously resemble dream-vines that bloom in stranger corners. She won't say where she sources them, only smiles when asked and rearranges a vase with absolute focus."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0016","type":"heading3","text":"\"Ombre\" the Showman"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0017","type":"paragraph","text":"A street shadow-puppeteer whose enacted stories have a peculiar habit of coming true. He seems harmless, charming even, but there's something faintly wrong about how his hands move, how the shadows linger longer than light should allow. He performs in the gas-lit margins of the Boulevard (@new-miri-urban), always just outside the reach of the nearest lamp."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0018","type":"heading3","text":"Poll Amaya"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0019","type":"paragraph","text":"An OrangeVibe streamer, loud and follower-obsessed, always chasing the next viral moment. Perpetually scooping or heckling the crew, seeing their mysterious work as a goldmine for content—if only she could figure out what they're actually doing."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0020","type":"heading2","text":"The Outskirts & Fringe"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0021","type":"heading3","text":"Old Hei / 老黑"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0022","type":"paragraph","text":"The Outskirts scavenger and unlicensed guide. Once pulled @shopin out of the dead mall when the kid wandered too deep. Treats him like a stray—gruff, unsentimental, but shows up when it matters. Maintains a territorial understanding with Sergeant Tan."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0023","type":"heading3","text":"Madame Sévère"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0024","type":"paragraph","text":"Concession landlady and loan-shark with a gift for knowing everyone's debts. Both @aria and @adrian owe her rent. Patient, professional, remembers every single number owed to her, and collects with a smile."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0025","type":"heading3","text":"Tobias Wend"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0026","type":"paragraph","text":"Junior OrangeVibe clerk who processes listings from the back office. He handled the \"Beneath the Moon\" post and has been unnerved ever since—the poster's account doesn't trace back to any user he can find. It's as if the listing materialized from nowhere. See @an-orange-problem."},{"id":"b-nmsl-0027","type":"heading3","text":"Sister Yun / 云修女"},{"id":"b-nmsl-0028","type":"paragraph","text":"Ex-cult street preacher who works the market side handing out flyers that nobody quite reads. She recognizes something in @aria that she can't place—a quality that makes her pause mid-sentence and study the other woman's face with an intensity that feels like remembering."}]}

title: First Night
body: {"v":2,"blocks":[{"id":"b-fn-0001","type":"paragraph","text":"The corner still smells like disinfectant and rust, even years later. @aria makes it three steps past the boarded entrance before her hands start, and @adrian pretends not to notice the way she's gripping the gear bag like it might run. Inside, someone's already strung work lights across the lobby — harsh white pools that make the spray-painted warnings on the walls look fresh. This is the place @waterfront-precinct spent two weeks scrubbing from the news, and now they're being paid to film it."},{"id":"b-fn-0002","type":"paragraph","text":"@harriet doesn't turn when they enter, just calls over her shoulder: \"Gaffer?\" Her voice echoes wrong in the gutted space, like the walls remember when it was full. Adrian's badge instinct says medical examiner, the way she's cataloging sight lines — but he killed that instinct years ago."},{"id":"b-fn-0003","type":"paragraph","text":"@shopin is outside when they circle back for the cables, cross-legged on the sidewalk with a field journal, sketching the building's south face in blue pen. Every window, every fire escape, mapped like a blueprint. His eyes catch on Aria's hands, still shaking, half a second — and then he's back to his journal like she's not there."},{"id":"b-fn-0004","type":"paragraph","text":"No one's said a name yet. Everyone is pretending this is normal. The envelope is taped to the operating-room door — the room at the end of the hall, where the light doesn't reach. Inside: the second half of the pay, and four names in the same clean hand from the notes."},{"id":"b-fn-0005","type":"paragraph","text":"Aria recognizes the room before she sees the bolts. The table is gone, but the floor remembers — four anchor points still drilled into concrete. She hasn't stood here since the night the locks clicked and her father's voice said Hide, child. @adrian sees her freeze. He doesn't say anything, the same not-seeing he chose the first time, only now it's a kindness with a different weight."},{"id":"b-fn-0006","type":"paragraph","text":"They take the money. @harriet counts her share without comment. @shopin folds his into his journal like a bookmark. Nobody proposes leaving, and nobody proposes anything else. Staying is the agreement."},{"id":"b-fn-0007","type":"paragraph","text":"The work lights hum in the silence. Outside, the city pretends this building doesn't exist. Inside, four people are being paid to remember it does."}]}

title: The Orange Concession (橙租界)
body: {"v":2,"blocks":[{"id":"b-oc-0001","type":"paragraph","text":"When the empire-era powers carved up @new-miri-urban, the old cadastral surveyors didn't bother naming their slices — they just inked them in colors on the harbor map. The wealthiest, gas-lit heart of the city, the Boulevard, went down in orange ink, and the name stuck to everything that lived inside its lines. Say 'Orange' in New Miri today and nobody thinks of the fruit stalls — they think of a currency, a court, a stamp on a passport, and a very particular kind of trouble."},{"id":"b-oc-0002","type":"heading2","text":"The Color Map / 色图"},{"id":"b-oc-0003","type":"paragraph","text":"Three flags once flew over three unequal slices of the same harbor. Each brought its own law, its own bank, its own idea of a proper boulevard, and stamped its color onto the surveyors' map before anyone thought to ask the city's older bones what they wanted. Those bones won anyway — the indigenous skeleton under every concession's imported skin never went away, it just learned to wear a beret or a peacoat depending which color the block had been painted that decade."},{"id":"b-oc-0004","type":"paragraph","text":"Orange money still clears faster than any other currency at a Boulevard bank window. Orange papers still get you further at a checkpoint than papers stamped by either of its old rivals. The empires are gone, mostly, or thinned to consulates and shipping ledgers — but the paint never got scrubbed off the map, and neither did the habits it taught everyone."},{"id":"b-oc-0005","type":"heading2","text":"The Three Powers"},{"id":"b-oc-0006","type":"bullet","text":"**Orange — the Boulevard Authority (橙廷 Chéngtíng).** French-and-Italian-styled colonnades, gaslamp ordinances, an opera house nobody can afford to fill. Orange is old money pretending it was always here — gas-lit, mannered, and quietly terrified of anything it can't put a stamp on."},{"id":"b-oc-0007","type":"bullet","text":"**Cobalt — the Compact Maritime Concession (青海盟 Qīnghǎi Méng).** The rival power, a shipping-and-insurance consortium out of a cooler, foggier coastline, flying deep-blue house flags over its piers. Cobalt never wanted a boulevard — it wanted a harbor, a customs house, and nobody asking why its cargo manifests never quite add up. Cobalt law is maritime law wearing a landlord's hat."},{"id":"bullet-oc-0008","type":"bullet","text":"**The Outskirts (界外 Jièwài).** No single color, no single flag — the indigenous and immigrant-run fringe where Orange and Cobalt's writs simply stop meaning anything. Effectively unpoliced by either empire, which locals will tell you, deadpan, is the safest place in the city right up until it isn't."},{"id":"b-oc-0009","type":"heading2","text":"Law at the Curb"},{"id":"b-oc-0010","type":"paragraph","text":"Jurisdiction in the concessions was never drawn with a straight ruler, and a century on it still isn't. An officer's authority can run out mid-crosswalk. The clearest monument to the mess is the @waterfront-precinct itself — a single building that the old survey somehow split down the middle, so that its crowded civilian-facing left wing answers to different paperwork than its market-stall-lined right wing of Chinese, Japanese, and Southeast Asian vendors. Same roof, two colors of law, one very confused front desk."},{"id":"b-oc-0011","type":"paragraph","text":"This is precisely the geometry that ended @adrian's career. His raid on the hospital corner crossed a concession line mid-arrest — a hallway that started in one jurisdiction and ended in another — and it didn't matter that the arrest was clean. What mattered was which color the floor tile was under his boots when the cuffs went on. An ex-cop who's radioactive in one color of law is radioactive in all three; nobody wants to inherit a case Orange, Cobalt, and the Outskirts will each swear belonged to somebody else."},{"id":"b-oc-0012","type":"heading2","text":"Daily Life"},{"id":"b-oc-0013","type":"paragraph","text":"You learn the colors the way you learn traffic patterns — not from a book, from getting it wrong once. The exchange rate on a bowl of noodles can shift crossing a single street. A receipt an Orange landlord will honor is wastepaper three blocks into Cobalt territory. Streetlamps, gutters, who you call when something's actually wrong — all of it recolors block to block, and everybody carries a private mental map nobody else quite agrees with."},{"id":"b-oc-0014","type":"paragraph","text":"Even the gossip has a jurisdiction. OrangeVibe — the Boulevard's own flavor of StreamVibe, gas-lit and a little self-important — covers the concession's scandals, sales, and psychic hotline ads with the smug thoroughness of a paper that knows its readers can't leave the color they're standing in."},{"id":"b-oc-0015","type":"heading2","text":"An Orange Problem"},{"id":"b-oc-0016","type":"paragraph","text":"Ask three concession clerks whose desk a mess belongs on and you'll get three different answers pointing at each other — that's @an-orange-problem, the local idiom for trouble that falls squarely into the gaps between colors, the parts of the map where nobody's writ quite reaches. It's the phrase you reach for when a landlord dispute, a smuggling case, or a body turns up somewhere the survey forgot to color in."},{"id":"b-oc-0017","type":"paragraph","text":"It is also, unhelpfully, exactly where the Dream Layer likes to leak. Phosphor vines don't recognize cadastral ink any better than the old empires' surveyors recognized the city's indigenous bones, and the thin spots between waking and dreaming turn up with suspicious regularity in the ungoverned seams — the alley behind the split precinct, the customs shed nobody's claimed since the last Cobalt audit, the noodle stall whose receipts are honored nowhere. Everyone in New Miri has, at some point, muttered that a job smells like an Orange Problem before they've even worked out which color they're standing in — see also @money-is-in-the-dream for what happens once someone follows the smell all the way down."}]}
